speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe exactly where you feel this shooting pain and whether it worsens when you touch the area or try to wear an earring. How many days or weeks have passed since your tympanoplasty surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Recurrent Cholesteatoma

The history of recurrent ear infections, the specific nature of your "shooting" pain (which can mimic dental pain or be referred from the jaw), and the sensation of discomfort when wearing earrings 12 weeks post-tympanoplasty are highly suggestive of a new growth in the middle ear, likely a cholesteatoma. This can erode bone and irritate the ossicles or surrounding structures, causing pain even with normal jaw movement during eating. I need to confirm this before we consider further treatment or revision surgery.

REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy_Microscope (Right Ear)
REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT Temporal Bone (Right Side)
